clue.text: Extremely stout officer guarding fixtures in the States?

indicators.note: an officer guarding something stands round it, so his letters enclose the rest

parts.note: LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant
US is the United States
fixtures are matches, which are also called ties

explanation.surface: A very fat policeman is posted to watch over sporting events in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' puts the pieces inside the officer; 'fixtures' in the British sense of scheduled matches, often called ties in cup competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean robust or hearty, and the superlative of lusty means most vigorous and sturdy.

clue.text: Feel sorry for bird seen no longer in northern height

indicators.note: the bird is placed in the height, so its letters go inside the mountain's

parts.note: BEN is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
the moa was a huge flightless New Zealand bird, now extinct

explanation.surface: Someone mourns a bird that no longer appears on a Scottish peak.
explanation.definitionFit: To bemoan something is to lament or express regret over it.

clue.text: Following sting, queen's running temperature

parts.note: a sting is a swindle, a con

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of queen's are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: After being stung, the queen bee is running a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges QUEENS (the apostrophe gives no letter) into SEQUEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Consequent means resulting or coming after as an effect, a synonym of following.

clue.text: Reactionary opts for ditching Conservative leader

indicators.note: a reactionary goes backwards politically, so the word is read in reverse
ditching the Conservative means its letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: to opt for something is to pick it

explanation.surface: A right-wing figure chooses to get rid of the Tory party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' removes C from PICKS to leave PIKS; 'Reactionary' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A skip is the captain of a curling or bowls team, the player who leads it.

clue.text: Adjusted totals given for variable constituents

indicators.note: adjusted suggests these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: The election totals were revised because some voters changed their minds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusted' rearranges TOTALSGIVENFOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating voters are electors with no fixed party loyalty, so their support varies from one election to the next.

clue.text: Rob smuggled Spanish wine

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, so smuggled gives ran
sack is an old name for sherry and similar white wines from Spain

explanation.surface: A man called Rob brought in Spanish wine illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' reads as a man's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search it violently and plunder it, a way of robbing.

clue.text: Slightly raise pressure cutting dividend before noon

indicators.note: before places the cut word ahead of the letter for noon
pressure cutting the dividend means its letter splits that word

parts.note: a dividend is a share of profits
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A small increase in pressure cut into the shareholders' payout before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts P inside SHARE.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, to sharpen a note is to raise its pitch by a small amount, a semitone.

clue.text: Compassionate nurses quietly critical

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the first word holds the second inside

parts.note: a compassionate person is caring
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Kind nurses speak softly about their criticisms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like a noun but is the verb putting P inside CARING.
explanation.definitionFit: Carping describes petty, nagging fault-finding, so it means critical in a grumbling way.

clue.text: Last worker's left shifting gear

indicators.note: the letter for left is shifted to a new spot in the word

parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block a shoemaker uses, so a last worker is a cobbler

explanation.surface: The final employee has gone, taking his kit with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' suggests final, but it is the shoemaker's block; the L moves up to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing or personal belongings, the same as gear.

clue.text: Violinist's technique puts more icing on the cake perhaps

definitions.meaning: a way of bowing two strings at once to sound two notes together

definitions.text: puts more icing on the cake perhaps
definitions.meaning: read as ..., increasing what goes on top of a cake

explanation.definitionFit: Double stopping is pressing two strings at once on a bowed instrument; split differently it also reads as doubling a topping.

clue.text: Boss hit in recession

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to bonk is to hit, informally

explanation.surface: The manager has been hit hard by the economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in recession' turns BONK round.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round raised stud or knob, for example at the centre of a shield.

clue.text: Vital moment that could set the court alight?

definitions.text: Vital moment that could set the court alight?

parts.words: Vital moment that could set the court alight?
parts.note: the decisive moment in tennis, read as the tip of a match, the small stick that is struck to light a fire

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the point that can win the whole contest is critical, and a match's head is its point.

clue.text: Arthurian knight, a little over halfway back, remains

indicators.note: back tells us to read the shortened name in reverse
only a little more than half the knight's full title is kept

parts.note: Sir Bedivere was a knight of King Arthur's Round Table

explanation.surface: A knight of the Round Table, partly retreating, stays behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping six of the eleven letters of SIR BEDIVERE leaves SIRBED; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something broken or destroyed.

clue.text: Met government department principals in York, ending dispute

parts.note: DEFRA is the UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs

indicators.note: principals are the leading figures, so the first letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: Officials from a ministry come to York to settle an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To defray costs is to pay them, and to meet a bill means the same.

clue.text: Scratch force invades with more success, killing a thousand

indicators.note: force invades the word, so its letter goes inside
killing the thousand removes its letter

parts.note: luckier means having more good fortune
K stands for a thousand
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A scratch team pushes in and wins more, losing a thousand along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing' removes K from LUCKIER to leave LUCIER, and 'invades' puts F inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucifer is an old word for a friction match, the kind lit by scratching it.

clue.text: Star departs, one having timely drink

parts.note: the sun is a star
D is the abbreviation for departs on a timetable
an owner is one who has something

explanation.surface: A celebrity leaves, and someone has a drink right on time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is a drink taken at sunset, so its timing is part of the name.

clue.text: Sloth in tree briefly on the move meets another coming up

indicators.note: letters on the move are shifted into a new order
briefly means the word is cut short by a letter
in a down clue, coming up means the word reads upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: another sloth: the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: A sloth climbing a tree meets a second one heading up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts TREE to TRE, 'on the move' rearranges it to ERT, and 'coming up' reverses AI to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth here is the sin of laziness, and inertia is a reluctance to move or act.

clue.text: Special relations with trade union set up for Soviet high flyer

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the pieces read upwards, so they are reversed

parts.note: kin are one's relations

explanation.surface: A special family tie with the union was established for a Soviet star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns KINTU round to UTNIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik was the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957 into high orbit.

clue.text: Arrangement to join marshal at brothel

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military officer meets someone at a house of ill repute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'marshal' looks like a noun but is the verb rearranging ATBROTHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is an engagement, an agreement that two people will marry.

clue.text: Mum's sister on the Riviera hasn't got over physio, perhaps

parts.note: MA is mum, with the possessive S

indicators.note: the sister lacks the letter for over, so it is dropped

parts.note: soeur is the French word for sister, spoken on the French Riviera
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Mum's French sister is not yet over seeing a physiotherapist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't got' removes O from SOEUR to leave SEUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur gives massage, and a physiotherapist is one example of someone who might.

clue.text: Heard evidence of cold under discussion?

indicators.note: heard tells us the answer sounds like the word that follows

parts.note: atishoo is the sound of a sneeze, a sign of a cold

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sneeze is proof of a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: A tissue is itself evidence of a cold, adding a second layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being debated or considered.

clue.text: Extremists in capital mounting unchanged festival

parts.note: the extreme letters of the word capital are C and L, spelt out as C and L

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: something unchanged stays the same

explanation.surface: Radicals in the city stage a festival that never changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses SAME to EMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas is the Christian feast on 2 February marking the presentation of Christ in the Temple.

clue.text: Before start of year, local warranted promotion

indicators.note: before places those words ahead of the next letter

parts.note: in Britain the local is one's neighbourhood pub
licit means lawful or authorised

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of year

explanation.surface: Early in the year, the local has legitimate publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicity is the business of promoting something to the public.

clue.text: Ditching one side for the other, earnest European's not gone soft

indicators.text: Ditching one side for the other
indicators.note: one side, right, is dropped and the other side, left, put in its place

parts.note: ardent means passionate or earnest
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: An earnest European changes sides but has not become soft.
explanation.walkthrough: R for right becomes L for left in ARDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Al dente describes pasta cooked so that it is still firm to the bite.

clue.text: Sounder artisan?

parts.note: a craftsman who works with lead, read as one who sounds depths with a lead weight on a line

explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to measure depth with a lead weight, so one who sounds the depth is a plumb-er.

clue.text: Towel primarily for bachelor in changing room as protective cover

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a cubicle is a small room for changing clothes

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of towel

explanation.surface: Towels mainly for the single man in the changing room as a cover-up.
explanation.walkthrough: T replaces B in CUBICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuticle is the layer of skin at the base of a nail, protecting it.

clue.text: Mush fed to condemned man that's not good, in theory

indicators.note: the mush is fed into the man, so its letters go inside
the man without good means the letter is removed

parts.note: a goner is someone doomed
pap is soft mushy food

explanation.surface: The prisoner's last meal of mush is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'condemned man' suggests a prisoner, but the doomed one is any person who is done for; 'that's not' drops the G, and 'fed to' puts the mush inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle or as planned but may not in practice.

clue.text: Republican with vision but no capital fixed

indicators.note: no capital means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: sighted means able to see

explanation.surface: A Republican with vision but no money mended things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no capital' drops the first letter S from SIGHTED.
explanation.definitionFit: To right a wrong is to correct it, so righted means put right or repaired.
